title: table-chart-analyzer output
description: Schema for the JSON object returned by the table-chart-analyzer subagent (Phase 2c — Deep Table/Chart Understanding). The orchestrator validates every response against this schema before appending to workspace/element_understanding.jsonl and splitting the questions[] into workspace/question_queue.jsonl. One record per data-driven table/chart element (or per cross-deck sample group when multiple instances are analyzed together).

element_id.description: The element_id of the representative (richest) instance, copied verbatim from the input. Null only in the error-fallback case.

member_element_ids.description: When multiple samples of the same table/chart were analyzed together, every instance's element_id (including element_id above). Single-sample analysis may omit this or list just the one id.

shape.description: What was deeply analyzed. 'image' = flattened content with NO render/crop available — structure could not be read from the object model OR from pixels (the only remaining unreadable case).

data_category.description: The investment-data-category, echoed from the Phase-2a classification prior (refine only with strong evidence). Null for an unreadable image or reference-other ambiguity. Same enum as the element-classifier.

authoring_component.description: The Assette authoring primitive, echoed from Phase 2a but REFINED with the structural evidence (e.g. promote smart-shell:table to smart-shell:zigzag once the observed max row count is known). Same enum as the element-classifier.

samples_analyzed.description: How many instances of this element were compared. 1 = single-sample (variance unknown, lean on priors + questions); >1 = multi-sample variance was computed.

readable.description: True when a structure record exists that downstream may bind against — read from the object model (inventory cells/series) OR from a rendered page/crop image (vision) OR both (mixed); structure_provenance records which. False only when neither is available (flattened image with no render) — in that case populate questions[] and do NOT fabricate structure.

structure_provenance.description: How the emitted structure was read. object-model: deterministically from inventory cells/series (high trust). vision: from a rendered page/crop image — structure only, values are illustrative. mixed: real extracted text inside vision-located geometry, or native + image samples combined. Provenance describes the structure you DID emit — a readable:false record (no structure) stamps object-model/deterministic. Records written before this field existed default to object-model.

verification.description: deterministic: machine-read structure, no human confirmation needed. needs-confirmation: vision-derived (vision|mixed provenance) — a human must confirm the structure before the Shell/Data Object is finalized. Records written before this field existed default to deterministic.

table.description: Present (non-null) iff shape == 'table' AND readable == true — whether the structure came from the object model or a rendered image is recorded in structure_provenance.

orientation.description: rows-are-records: each data row is one entity (a holding, a trade). rows-are-measures: each row is a named metric (risk-stats table). matrix: a true cross-tab.

columns.description: One entry per column, left to right. The per-column role + format + growth IS the core deliverable downstream Data Object / Smart Shell authoring binds to.

role.description: row-key: identifies the row (Security, Metric). label: a fixed text label. measure: a numeric data-bound value. dimension: a grouping dimension (Sector, Asset Class). derived: computed from other columns (Total, Excess). marker: a footnote/superscript marker column.

growth.description: fixed: this column is always present. grows-per-period: one such column is added each period (e.g. a calendar-year column added yearly). grows-per-entity: column set varies per account/product/mandate. conditional: present only in some contexts.

kind.description: fixed-set: a known fixed set of rows (risk metrics, period rows). repeating-group: one row per data record, count varies (holdings, transactions). mixed: a repeating group plus fixed header/subtotal/total rows.

group_dimension.description: When rows are grouped/subtotalled, the dimension they group by (e.g. Sector). Null when ungrouped.

conditional_formatting.description: Row/cell-specific formatting the rendered sample implies. NOTE: the inventory does NOT carry cell fills/fonts/colors, so this is INFERRED from cell text (e.g. parenthesised or signed negatives) or ASKED — set evidence accordingly.

evidence.description: observed: read from cell text (e.g. '(0.22%)' negatives). observed-render: seen in the rendered image (e.g. negatives drawn in red) — vision CAN legitimately see formatting the inventory cannot, but must mark it as render-sourced. inferred: domain prior. asked: surfaced as a question because neither the inventory nor a render can show it.

volume.description: bounded: a Top-N / fixed-height table (-> smart-shell:table). full-list: a long list that wraps across columns/slides (-> smart-shell:zigzag).

footnote_markers.description: Superscript / symbol markers in headers or cells that tie to footnote text (e.g. '1', '*', 'GIPS').

chart.description: Present (non-null) iff shape == 'chart' AND readable == true — whether the structure came from the object model or a rendered image is recorded in structure_provenance.

chart_type.description: LINE / PIE / COLUMN / BAR / AREA / ... (python-pptx enum name) or 'unknown'.

variance_findings.description: What the multi-sample comparison revealed (empty when samples_analyzed == 1). Each finding maps an observed difference/constancy across instances to a structural inference — this is how dynamic-vs-structural is DECIDED rather than guessed.

observation.description: What differed or stayed constant across the samples.

vision_source_images.description: vision/mixed provenance only: the crop/render image path(s) you actually Read to derive the structure, copied verbatim from the samples' vision blocks. The auto-queued confirm question and the build-time verification gate point humans at these so they can compare the claimed structure against the pixels.

dynamic_field_candidates.description: Columns / dimensions that should likely become shared Dynamic Fields downstream (e.g. Sector, As of Date, Benchmark Name). Richer than the classifier's single routing_hint.

system_block_candidates.description: System blocks the structure implies (e.g. Sectors, Asset Classes, Countries, Currency Codes, As of Dates, Account/Product Master). Configure-only — never scaffold custom.

confidence.description: Honest confidence in the deep-understanding record. Lower it when single-sample, when key facts were guessed, or when blocking questions remain. Below 0.7 routes to review alongside any blocking questions.

rationale.description: Two to five sentences: how the structure was read, what the samples showed, and what the open questions hinge on.

questions.description: Active clarifying questions for the implementer — the Phase 2c HITL primitive. Ask ONLY what cannot be inferred from the sample(s) and matters downstream (see the deep-table-chart-understanding skill's ASK-vs-infer rule). Empty array when the structure is fully resolved.

options.description: Candidate answers when the choice is a closed set (e.g. ['Top-N display', 'Full list']). Free-form answer expected when omitted/empty.

default.description: The best-guess answer to assume if the implementer does not respond (keeps the pipeline moving). Null when there is no safe default.

why.description: One line: what downstream decision this answer changes (Shell type, Data Object shaping, disclosure pairing).

blocking.description: True when scaffolding cannot proceed correctly without an answer (compliance basis, dynamic structure). Blocking questions gate Phase 3 regardless of confidence.
